name: StepSecurity Harden-Runner
author: StepSecurity

amendments.append: A job that runs an AI agent on untrusted event content also limits runner egress to an allow-list in block mode, for example `step-security/harden-runner` pinned by SHA with `egress-policy: block`, explicit `allowed-endpoints` and `disable-telemetry: true`, or a self-hosted runner behind the CFG-1 network allow-list. Audit mode only observes traffic, so it doesn't remove AGT-4's outbound leg.

notes: Not installed in this repo by the scout. The action downloads a pinned agent binary (step-security/agent v0.18.1 or agent-ebpf v1.9.6), checks its SHA-256 and runs it as a root systemd service. It sends job events to *.stepsecurity.io unless telemetry is disabled. The free Community tier covers only public repos on GitHub-hosted runners: private repos and self-hosted/ARC runners need the paid tier, which is why the amendment also allows a network-layer allow-list.
rationale: Distilled into AGT-6 as one way to remove AGT-4's outbound leg in CI. AGT-4 asks for an egress allow-list and CFG-1 restricts host egress, but nothing told an agent workflow how to block egress on a GitHub runner. Harden-Runner is the most widely used open action that enforces it, and its blocklist caught tj-actions/changed-files (CVE-2025-30066). zizmor (SEC-17) lints workflow text but can't block traffic at runtime, so the two complement each other. pipelab-org/pipelock (watch, 68) covers local agent egress rather than CI runners, where the pinned anthropic-sandbox-runtime already applies.
